bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "We maintained our debt-free status and further strengthened our liquidity position, with cash and cash equivalents increasing to approximately ₹69.9 crore as of March 31, 2026"; the Chairman cites a "debt-free balance sheet, healthy liquidity position, and disciplined approach to working capital management".
- Net Debt/Equity (deck definition: (LT Debt + ST Debt)/Total Equity): FY23 1.17, FY24 0.67, FY25 -0.17, FY26 -0.35.
- Balance sheet shows nil borrowings: Non-current Borrowings 0.00 across Mar'24/Mar'25/Mar'26 and Current Borrowings 43.49 (Mar'24) → 4.27 (Mar'25) → 0.00 (Mar'26).
- Working capital: Inventories Rs. 120.69 cr and Trade receivables Rs. 72.42 cr as on 31 Mar'26 (vs 125.41 and 84.98 as on 31 Mar'25); the Chairman states "We delivered improved cash flows and a more efficient working capital cycle during the year."
- Falling but still high return ratios: ROE 96% (FY23), 59% (FY24), 25% (FY25), 13% (FY26); ROCE 98%, 64%, 28%, 14% over the same years. The deck offers no dividend policy or payout data.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Sarees (89.3% of revenue); Kurtis & Dress Materials (7.4%); Blouse Pieces (1.5%); Shirt & Pant Pieces (0.9%); Others (0.9%); Kolhapur store contributes 84.6% of store revenue.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- "Saraswati Saree Depot Limited (SSDL), a major sarees wholesaler... IS ONE OF INDIA'S LEADING PLAYER IN THE B2B SEGMENT of this Industry"; described as "One of India's leading organized saree wholesalers, growing strong over three decades".
- Customer and supplier concentration are both low: "The top 10 suppliers account for less than 26% of total purchases" and "The top 10 customers contribute to less than 8% of total sales".
- Geographic base is southern and western India: "SSDL primarily sells in southern and western regions, including Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu, serving over 13,000 unique customers in fiscal 2024."
- Industry backdrop cited from Crisil: the organized saree sector is "growing at a 9-10% CAGR" and "is expected to constitute 32-37% of the market by fiscal 2029, up from 25-30% currently", with the overall industry projected to grow at a "5-6% CAGR from fiscal 2024 to 2029, reaching Rs. 650-675 billion by fiscal 2029".
- Brand/recognition claims: recipient of "Star of the Industry", "Iconic Brand" and the "Achievers of South Maharashtra" award from the Times of India.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demand guidance] The Chairman guides to a materially weaker year ahead: "we expect demand conditions in the coming year to remain significantly weaker than the levels witnessed in recent years, reflecting continued softness in consumer spending and a cautious market environment."
- [Promoter-led management] The board is family-led — Shankar Dulhani (Chairman & Executive Director, 38 years in the industry), Vinod Dulhani (MD & CEO, 27+ years, second generation), Mahesh Dulhani and Rajesh Dulhani (Executive Directors, 30 and 29 years).
- [Founding-year conflict] The deck states two different origins: "BEGAN IN 1966" in the company overview, while the Timeline says the promoters "formally launched a partnership firm" in 1993 "After three decades in the saree industry".
- [Long-run growth] "The company's REVENUE GREW FROM Rs. 222.9 CRORE IN FY2014 to SALES EXCEEDING Rs. 600 CRORE IN FY2024, GENERATING A CAGR OF 10.4% OVER THIS PERIOD."
- [Industry cycle] Crisil-sourced: the saree industry was Rs. 558 billion in fiscal 2020, "fell by ~43% in fiscal 2021 due to pandemic-related store closures", "rebounded by ~44% in fiscal 2022", and by fiscal 2024 is valued at Rs. 515 billion, "reflecting ~5% growth from the previous year".

deepdive.thesis: Saraswati Saree Depot is a leading organized wholesale player in India's saree market with a strong brand, debt-free balance sheet, and 300,000+ SKUs, but faces margin pressure from rising procurement costs and soft consumer demand. Its strategic retail entry and Surat procurement office offer long-term growth levers amid industry formalization.
